drafted_from: tools/documents-as-list-rows/tool-rows.json (tool:split-a-document-into-item-documents), read-data/split.mjs, do-work/documents.mjs and test/documents-as-list-rows.test.mjs (the JSON list split); run on a made-up folder
start_here: Say to your AI: "Split my garden notes in /tmp/garden-notes into one document per plant using the mapping file mapping.json, and check it first." It reads the tool row, runs the split with --check, then into an empty folder, and shows you the item documents.
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it reads a mapping and documents in a folder and writes item documents and a leftover folder, keeping no rows.
instructions: 1. Put the documents and a mapping.json in one folder (root). For a JSON list the mapping is {"sources":[{"name":"garden","file":"garden.json"}],"items_at":"plants","id":"{name}-{#}"}; for markdown it names a heading and row pattern with an (?<id>...) group.

2. Say "Split my documents into one per item"; your AI reads the row with tools:list and runs the command with --check in place of --out and --leftover. Read the report: items, lines or items read, leftover.
3. Run it again with --out plants --leftover rest, into a folder that does not exist yet or is empty (a used folder is refused).
4. Open two or three of the item documents (plants/basil-1.md) and the leftover (rest/garden.json) with your AI before anything else changes.

worked_examples.title: Split a JSON list of two plants into one document each
worked_examples.ask: Split my garden notes into one document per plant, checking first.
worked_examples.given: Read from tools/documents-as-list-rows/read-data/split.mjs and checked against the JSON-list case of test/documents-as-list-rows.test.mjs, and run on a made-up folder. In /tmp/garden-notes, garden.json is {"about":"made-up garden notes","plants":[{"name":"basil","water":"daily","sun":6},{"name":"mint","water":"weekly","sun":3}]} and mapping.json is {"sources":[{"name":"garden","file":"garden.json"}],"items_at":"plants","id":"{name}-{#}","field_order":["name"]}. The AI then runs: node tools/documents-as-list-rows/do-work/documents.mjs split --root /tmp/garden-notes --mapping mapping.json --out plants --leftover rest
worked_examples.hands_back: The last line printed is {"items":2,"items_in":2,"leftover_documents":1}. plants/basil-1.md holds the frontmatter id: basil-1, name: basil, sun: 6, water: daily (the field_order field first, the rest sorted); plants/mint-2.md is the same for mint; rest/garden.json holds {"about":"made-up garden notes"}. With --check in place of --out and --leftover it prints the same line and writes nothing.
